text:
BMO Field broke ground on marzo 29, 2006 and opened on abril 28, 2007, built as a soccer-specific stadium for the 2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup and as the first home of Toronto FC. Its original construction cost was CA$62.9 million, and it was designed by Brisbin Brooks Beynon Architects.

The ground was originally surfaced with FieldTurf from 2007 to 2009, a playing surface that drew player criticism. It was converted to natural Kentucky bluegrass before the 2010 season, and then to a hybrid-grass system from 2019.

A major expansion designed by Gensler followed in 2014–2016, costing roughly CA$120 million. It added an east-grandstand upper deck of about 8,400 seats, completed in mayo 2015, along with a canopy roof over the east, west and south stands and a lengthened field for Canadian football. Together these works raised soccer capacity from around 21,566 to roughly 30,000.

The stadium's identity widened beyond soccer when the CFL's Toronto Argonauts moved in for the 2016 season. Beyond its regular configuration, which seats 28,180, the venue has long hosted finals and showcase fixtures, reflecting its standing as a national football home.

Bank of Montreal holds the naming rights as BMO Field, but the stadium is temporarily renamed Toronto Stadium for the 2026 World Cup under FIFA's clean-venue policy — just as it was branded National Soccer Stadium for the 2007 and 2014 FIFA youth tournaments. For the 2026 World Cup it hosts six matches: five group-stage games plus one Round of 32 fixture on julio 2, 2026, among them Canada's opener on junio 12, 2026. Its tournament capacity is set at 43,036.
